answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token bond before it may submit work, with rewards released only after independent, randomly assigned peers verify the result. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund every hollow identity separately, and coordinated false approvals risk slashing those bonds. The orchard of identities may look broad, but its cost grows with each funded account; cheap account creation alone cannot buy influence across the canyon of scarce stake and verification.
